helpful: The provisioned application.txt was complete and readable; it carried the whole of the applicant's case.
CourtListener read_document on the Sixth Circuit opinion gave the facts the application understates.
The statpack interim section's per-Term counts were enough to compute the strictly-prior pooled rate.
gaps: The government's response in opposition is the entry that opened this event, but it was not provisioned under record/documents/; a response-filed cell should get the response text alongside the application.
WebFetch returns raw PDF bytes for supremecourt.gov DocketPDF links; a PDF-to-text step in the fetcher would save a local extraction detour.
No conditioned interim cut exists for 'response requested' or 'private criminal-defendant applicant', so the ladder and applicant-class adjustments were judgment, not table reads.
notes: fedcourts query with --include-applications ranks by recency, so it surfaced extension applications rather than comparable stay applications; a --application-kind filter would make it useful for interim cells.
